hints: Notice you are given two loaded lengths, $90\text{ mm}$ and $115\text{ mm}$, but not the unstretched length, so you cannot find extension directly from one reading.
Recall Hooke's law as $F = kx$, so for two loads the unknown natural length cancels if you use the differences $\Delta F = k\Delta x$.
Calculate $\Delta F = 1.30 - 0.80$ in $\text{N}$ and $\Delta x = 115 - 90$ in $\text{mm}$, convert $\Delta x$ to $\text{m}$, then evaluate $k = \Delta F / \Delta x$.
walkthrough: Write Hooke's law for each state: $F_1 = k(L_1 - L_0)$ and $F_2 = k(L_2 - L_0)$, where $L_0$ is the unknown natural length.
Subtract to eliminate $L_0$: $F_2 - F_1 = k(L_2 - L_1)$, so $k = \Delta F / \Delta x$.
Find the changes: $\Delta F = 1.30 - 0.80 = 0.50\text{ N}$ and $\Delta L = 115 - 90 = 25\text{ mm}$.
Convert length change to metres: $\Delta x = 25\text{ mm} = 0.025\text{ m}$.
Substitute: $k = 0.50 / 0.025 = 20\text{ N m}^{-1}$ with units of force per unit extension. This is option D.

options.A: Divides $0.80\text{ N}$ by the total length $0.090\text{ m}$ to get about $8.9\text{ N m}^{-1}$, but Hooke's law uses extension from natural length, not total length.
options.B: Uses about $10\text{ N m}^{-1}$ from combining the two loads and lengths incorrectly, instead of using the change in force divided by the change in length.
options.C: Divides $1.30\text{ N}$ by the total length $0.115\text{ m}$ to get about $11\text{ N m}^{-1}$, which again mistakes the measured length for the extension.
options.D: The change $0.50\text{ N}$ divided by the change $0.025\text{ m}$ gives $20\text{ N m}^{-1}$, which is the true spring constant.
